subject: Private offer: term and buyer approval alignment — Westfield Health
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@westfield-health.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@westfield-health.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private offer inquiry - term and approval routing

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for taking this — Samir (procurement) and I are reviewing options for an AWS private offer for our telemetry/embedding usage. Two quick questions to unblock internal routing:

1) If we agree to a 24-month term, can Redwood provide a steeper pricing band vs 12 months (we need numbers to pitch to our CFO)?
2) For private-offer activation, who exactly needs to sign/approve on our side? Our procurement team wants a clear list (procurement, legal, CFO) so we can map the buyer approvers.

We also have a pilot that needs to start in ~6 weeks; is there flexibility on start/activation window?

Thanks — attaching our internal scoping note.

Best,
Ava
Director, Vendor Sourcing
Westfield Health

Attachments: WFH-scoping-note.docx (attachment stub)
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@westfield-health.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@westfield-health.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 12:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry - term and approval routing

Hi Ava / Samir — thanks for the clear questions. Quick summary and two options to help your CFO/procurement evaluate:

Option A — 12-month private offer (pilot-friendly):
- Monthly usage pricing baseline: $0.029 / 1K tokens (standard quantized profile)
- One-time onboarding credit: 5% of first-year usage (applied as invoice credit)
- Activation window: must activate the private offer within 90 days of signing

Option B — 24-month private offer (best unit economics):
- Monthly usage pricing baseline: $0.024 / 1K tokens (10% lower than 12m)
- One-time onboarding credit: 8% of first-year usage
- Activation window: activate within 120 days of signing; commit spreads risk across two years

Buyer approvals we typically see required on the customer side:
- Procurement (purchase order / private-offer acceptance)
- Legal (review of T&Cs or confirmation of marketplace terms)
- Finance/CFO (budget signoff for committed terms)

If you want, we can issue a private-offer PDF for both options so you can circulate to your approvers. I attached a short price comparison and a skeleton private-offer for review.

Next steps I suggest:
- Tell me which option you'd like formalized (A or B)
- Share the list of approvers and preferred signing order (procurement -> legal -> finance is common)
- We can then push a DocuSign envelope and a private-offer to AWS for activation (HubSpot deal updated once signed)

I'll loop in Grace and Vivek to coordinate activation timing and any implementation credit.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: price-breakdown-12vs24.xlsx; WFH-private-offer-draft.pdf (attachment stubs)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@westfield-health.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry - term and approval routing

Thanks Lukas — that breakdown helps. Two follow-ups from our side:

- Our CFO is reluctant to commit to 24 months without a phased ramp. Would Redwood consider a 9-month pilot as a bridge to a 24-month commitment (pilot pricing rolled into Year 1 if converted)?
- For legal, we'd like a clear activation clause: contract is effective on signature but the private-offer activation with AWS can be scheduled to start on a date we confirm (we may need a delay to line up procurement windows).

Quoted for context:
> Option B — 24-month private offer (best unit economics):
> - Monthly usage pricing baseline: $0.024 / 1K tokens (10% lower than 12m)
> - One-time onboarding credit: 8% of first-year usage
> - Activation window: activate within 120 days of signing; commit spreads risk across two years

If you can sketch a mutual action plan with signoff gates (pilot -> conversion -> activation), we can map our approvers and try to accelerate.

Samir
Senior Procurement Manager
Westfield Health
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@westfield-health.com>, Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@westfield-health.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry - term and approval routing

Samir — totally reasonable. Proposed mutual action plan below (we can convert to a shared doc / HubSpot task list):

MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (MAP)
1) Sign Pilot private offer (9 months) — Redwood issues pilot PO/private-offer PDF -> Westfield signs procurement + legal
2) Pilot execution (weeks 0-9): implementation + sample evals; weekly checkpoint with Grace (CS)
3) Conversion decision (week 8): if OK, Westfield signs addendum to convert pilot into a 24-month commitment; pricing gap from pilot to Year1 rolled into Year1 usage credits
4) AWS activation scheduling: upon conversion sign, Redwood files activation request with AWS; target activation window up to 60 days after conversion signature (we can extend if you need more runway)

Notes / constraints:
- We can formalize the pilot -> conversion pathway in the private-offer PDF; AWS allows addenda that specify conversion terms but it's important legal signs off on the addendum language.
- To protect unit economics, the 24-month pricing (Option B) requires a commitment signature that includes CFO approval; procurement-only signatures won't trigger the 24m pricing unless finance confirms the funding cadence.

Next actions I will take:
- Draft: (a) Pilot private-offer PDF and (b) a conversion addendum template (I'll attach both)
- Open a DocuSign envelope for signatures once you confirm the approver list and preferred order

Can you send the approver roster (name, role, email) and confirm whether procurement wants the pilot PO to be on Westfield letterhead or an AWS private-offer acceptance alone?

Regards,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: WFH-private-offer-v1.pdf; conversion-addendum-draft.docx (attachment stubs)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private offer inquiry - term and approval routing (internal)

Looping back with an internal recommendation before we send the DocuSign:

- Agree to the pilot -> 24m conversion path. Pilot at the 12m price band for months 1-9, then if converted apply the 24m pricing to the remainder of Year1 and Year2. That keeps the CFO comfortable.
- Request: ask for an extra 5% implementation credit if Westfield converts to 24m within 75 days of pilot sign — reduces friction for their procurement team (we can treat as one-time credit).
- Activation window: set to 60 days after conversion signature. If they need more, we'll approve on a case-by-case basis but require finance signoff.

I'll prepare a short cover note for the DocuSign envelope and mark the HubSpot deal (WFH-2026-045) with the MAP and credit ask. Vivek — please confirm you're OK with the 5% implementation credit and I will send to Lukas to attach to the offer PDF.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
